prompts.purpose: 整体重排跳台与顶部操作区
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: corrected game-level concept illustration.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Preserve its approved watercolor palette, moderately softened background, foreground clarity, exact framing and orthographic side-view camera. Modify ONLY the three small climbing platforms and the upper seed trough's standing arrangement. This is a precise level-layout correction, not a style redesign.

CURRENT PROBLEM:
The lowest small platform floats mostly above the left water gap; all three platforms are cluttered with pots and flowers; the upper trough has no usable place to stand on its right. Correct these issues while preserving the middle-island puzzle.

DESIRED CLIMBING ROUTE:
The three stepping ledges must sit entirely ABOVE THE MIDDLE ISLAND footprint, to the LEFT of the large folded green guide leaf. Arrange a compact upward switchback: middle-island ground -> first low ledge -> second ledge up-right -> third ledge up-left -> a short jump right to the high trough and its right-side standing deck. These are small simple flat masonry/terracotta ledges with root brackets, not broad staircases. There must be exactly THREE small climbing ledges, each distinct and unobstructed.
Use these approximate bounds in the 1859 x 846 reference image as spatial guidance (do not render measurements):
- Existing middle-island ground runs about x644–1088 with top y558. Keep this island unchanged.
- Remove the OLD lowest platform at approximately x558–675, y445, including its old root support and flowers; restore the pale background behind it. No leftover foothold over the water.
- NEW low ledge: approximately x650–740, top y435. Its whole walkable width lies above the middle island. Thin slab, about 10–12 pixels thick; underside ends safely ABOVE the golden beam at y468. No roots or trailing plants below it blocking the beam.
- NEW second ledge: approximately x755–835, top y345, a short jump up-right of the first. Keep it to the left of the folded leaf silhouette, with a visible gap. 
- NEW third ledge: approximately x650–745, top y255, a short jump back up-left of the second. From here the player can jump right toward the upper trough. 
The three ledges are visually in the SAME gameplay plane as the island, not blurred into the distant wall. Keep the walkable upper surfaces clear and level. Remove the decorative terracotta pot, tall weeds and flowers FROM their standing surfaces. Put only a few small moss tufts at side edges or on very short supporting brackets. Preserve clear room above each landing, recognizable front edges, and separate silhouettes. No vines, support beams or platforms across either water gap.

UPPER TROUGH AND OPERATING DECK:
Keep the existing upper structure's overall footprint approximately x839–1050, but repartition it:
- Left section x839–965 is the shallow EMPTY seed trough, with low retaining lips, a small visible discharge opening feeding the existing curved root chute, and room for a seed to roll.
- Right section x965–1050 is a clearly FLAT EMPTY STANDING DECK, at the same height as the trough's inner floor (approximately y235–245). It has enough room for the tiny spirit to stand beside the seed and push left. This is a walkable root/wood shelf, not a high pot rim. Lower/remove the tall right post and decorative side obstruction that would prevent contact with the seed. Keep a low seed-retaining lip.
- Keep the operating deck ending LEFT of the vertical brown rope around x1065 and well LEFT of the central root wall. It does not connect to the far bank or bypass the root barrier.
- The seed trough is EMPTY because this illustration shows the solved state. Do not add another seed or duplicate the character.

STRICT INVARIANTS:
Keep the approved background brightness and watercolor detail EXACTLY like image 1: muted terracotta, warm ochre, sage foliage, soft blue-gray shadows. Do not wash it out further or make it darker/more detailed.
Keep left/right banks, two broad unbridged water gaps, middle island, folded green guide leaf and its hinge, control handle, seedpod in the plate's left cup, empty charging area, both pulley wheels and matte brown ropes, central root screen and raised leaf shutter, tiny open aperture, two mirrors, pale beast belly with dark target scale, the one tiny spirit on the right bank, pipe exit, foliage canopy and scene dimensions.
Keep the complete golden beam at its original path and thickness, uninterrupted through the root aperture. No newly placed platform, support or dangling vegetation may intersect this beam.
The folded guide leaf is not a stepping stone. Keep it visually separate from the three fixed platforms.
No arrows, numbers, labels, legends, dashed routes, UI, measurement marks or comparison panels. Output one finished corrected watercolor scene.

prompts.prompt:

There are THREE small bare stone ledges to the left of the folded green leaf. They form the climbing route. In this draft the lowest and highest ledges are STILL too far left, hanging above the water. Move these ledges RIGHT so ALL THREE are entirely above the solid middle island. MIDDLE ledge: x775 to x860, flat top y345, bottom y357.
HIGH ledge: x685 to x770, flat top y270, bottom y282.

Draw exactly THREE NEW ledges at the new positions. Thin, clean, flat landing surfaces, no pots, no flowers on top. Tiny moss at side edges only. Add short rear wall/root brackets that do not block the golden beam at y468. The lowest support must end above y452. The high and low ledges are vertically aligned; the middle one is offset right, making an obvious short upward switchback. Keep a clearly empty right-hand standing zone for the spirit to push the seed leftward. Preserve the existing outside footprint of this top structure, and its curved root chute. Preserve all unmentioned parts exactly, including the three large banks, both wide water gaps, light path, foreground, existing pale watercolor background strength, central root screen and leaf shutter, pulleys/ropes, mirror positions, seedpod on pressure plate, right-bank spirit, beast belly and feeding scale.
